messages:
jamie.nguyen: FYI customer (MegaPay) sent a SOC2 questionnaire asking for evidence of our patching timeline for CVE-2026-4210 in libfastcrypto (transitive via our tokenization lib). They also asked whether a KMS rotation last week could have affected signatures and whether we can rollback the runtime update we pushed yesterday. Need answers + artifact for SOC2.

lina: Got it. Drop the CVE link and the customer wording here and I'll triage. Also which deployment type? hosted/dedicated/private?

jamie.nguyen: Private (VPC) in eu-west-1, customer id MP-442. They have our runtime 2.3.1 (includes libtoken v1.8.0 -> libfastcrypto v2.0.1). KMS rotation recorded 2026-03-10 02:14 UTC per audit logs.

owen: Quick note: rollback of runtime is possible via deployment pinning + canary we have. But rollback won't change historical KMS rotation events — you can't retroactively re-sign. Provide audit log extracts and a signed statement for the customer.

sec-bot: Policy link: https://internal.redwood/security/patching#cve-triage and automated scan report: https://ci.internal.redwood/scans/scan-9876

lina: Triage summary: CVE-2026-4210 affects libfastcrypto <=2.0.3. Our runtime 2.3.1 includes libfastcrypto 2.0.1 -> vulnerable. Description: RCE via malformed crypto blob when parsing signatures. Exploit complexity: moderate; requires crafted request to inference endpoint. CVSS ~8.2. Recommendation: urgent/high.

lina: Mitigations and immediate steps:
- Preferred: patch to libfastcrypto 2.0.4 (backport for 2.0.x) and ship hotfix. ETA for PR + unit tests: ~6 hours.
- Temporary mitigation: add WAF rule to block malformed signature patterns and cap request body length.
- If customer prefers, we can rollback runtime to 2.2.9 while validating patch.

lina: Example commands for devs/CI:
```
# go mod edit -require github.com/fastcrypto v2.0.4
make deps-update && make test-integration
```

WAF example (edge mitigation):
```
aws wafv2 update-web-acl --scope REGIONAL --id wacl-0123 --rules '[{"Name":"bad-signature-block","Priority":5,"Action":{"Block":{}},"Statement":{"ByteMatch":{"SearchString":"\\x00\\x00\\x00","PositionalConstraint":"CONTAINS"}}}]'
```

lina: For private deployments we can push a hotfix package and coordinate with customer ops; no code change in customer app required.

sre-oncall: Rollback plan: we can pin the node group to runtime 2.2.9 and perform a rolling restart with a 2-node canary. Command example:
```
redwoodctl deploy set-runtime --cluster mp-442 --version 2.2.9 --canary 2
```
Expected downtime: none; tail latency may spike for a few minutes. Need approval before scheduling.

caroline: For SOC2 evidence we'll need:
- Signed timeline with timestamps (detection, triage, remediation, deploys)
- SBOM snapshots (before/after) in SPDX format
- Audit log extract for KMS rotation events and deployment events
I can assemble the bundle once you provide scan report, PR link, deploy IDs, and the sbom.

jamie.nguyen: I'll collect deploy IDs and link PR once created. Customer also asked whether KMS rotation could have invalidated past signatures — they're concerned offline signatures will fail after rotation.

lina: Short answer: key rotation can affect verification if they rely on a single key id. We use per-tenant envelope keys and rotate with a grace period; our verifier checks the key version encoded in the signature and falls back to previous versions for 30 days. Example audit log lines to include:
```
2026-03-10T02:14:21Z KMS RotateKey: keyId=arn:aws:kms:eu-west-1:...:key/abcd1234 previousKey=arn:...:key/oldabcd
2026-03-10T02:15:00Z SecretsManager UpdateSecret: secretId=tenant/mp-442/envelope-key -> newKeyId=arn:...
```
Rotation should not retroactively break verification within the fallback window; confirm retention policy.

owen: Lina, confirm KMS retention and whether verifier retains old public keys. If not, we need a reconciliation/re-sign flow for the customer.

lina: Confirmed: our KMS policy retains prior key material for 180 days; verifier falls back to previous versions for 30 days by default. That means signatures older than 30 days may not verify without re-signing. We'll include this in the SOC2 statement as a limitation and describe compensating controls.

samir: I'll coordinate the private hotfix push and propose a maintenance window if customer wants us to do an in-place hotfix. Draft customer message:
"Hi — we identified a vuln in a transitive crypto library affecting your private runtime. Recommended actions: 1) Apply hotfix (canary first) with no expected downtime; 2) Or rollback to 2.2.9 while we validate. KMS rotation does not invalidate signatures issued within 30 days; older signatures may require re-signing. Hotfix ETA: validation 6-12 hours"

caroline: Good. For SOC2 I'll need the raw scan output (machine readable), the PR diff, deploy job IDs, and the SBOM files. I'll prepare a template evidence zip and add placeholders. Also need wording for compensating control (WAF deployed).

lina: Opening PR now: https://git.internal.redwood/r/redwood/runtime/pulls/3742 -> unit tests green, integration pending. PR includes: patched dependency, changelog entry referencing CVE-2026-4210, and sbom generation script.

sre-oncall: Ack. I'll run the canary once integration finishes and monitor error-rate/latency. Will report back with deploy job IDs.

caroline: I'll draft the SOC2 evidence bundle and include the timeline and KMS audit log snippets. Once PR and deploy IDs are posted, I'll finalize and sign.

jamie.nguyen: Action items recap: lina triage + PR (ETA ~6h), samir coordinate hotfix with customer, sre-oncall standby for canary/rollback run, caroline prepare SOC2 evidence template and collect audit logs. I'll update customer with options in ~30m. :white_check_mark:

sec-bot: Additional scan note: 1 HIGH, 3 MEDIUM findings on private cluster mp-442. Report: https://ci.internal.redwood/scans/mp-442/2026-03-11

lina: PR link again: https://git.internal.redwood/r/redwood/runtime/pulls/3742 -> tagging @sre-oncall for canary run once integration completes.

sre-oncall: Standing by.

caroline: I'll attach placeholder SPDX and timeline by EOD.

jamie.nguyen: Thanks team, keep the convo in this thread for auditability and upload artifacts to the evidence bucket when ready.
